name: capell-app/widget-youtube
description: Your own poster image with a Play button, loading the YouTube video only when a visitor presses it.

marketplace.summary: YouTube videos on a page behind your own picture, with YouTube contacted only when a visitor presses play.
marketplace.description: On a page built in Layout Builder, paste a YouTube link, upload your own poster image to the Capell media library and give the video a title, which screen readers hear on the Play button. Visitors see your picture, and YouTube isn't contacted until they press play. The video then plays on the page in YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode, which cuts down tracking but doesn't stop it. If Privacy Centre is on and a visitor refused YouTube, they get a short message.
marketplace.problem: Standard YouTube videos slow my pages and contact YouTube before anyone chooses to watch.
marketplace.outcome: Pages open with your chosen picture, and the video plays in place on one tap.

faq.question: Does the page contact YouTube before someone plays the video?
faq.answer: No. A poster image you uploaded stands in for the video, and nothing is requested from YouTube until a visitor presses play.

faq.question: Do I need to upload my own poster image?
faq.answer: Yes. You upload a still image of your own, because the widget does not borrow YouTube's thumbnail. You also give the video a title, which screen readers read out.

faq.question: What if a visitor has turned down cookies?
faq.answer: If your site runs Privacy Centre and they turned down marketing cookies, or their browser asks sites not to track them, they see a short message and the video does not load.

faq.question: Does it remove YouTube's tracking?
faq.answer: No. It plays in YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode, which reduces tracking but does not remove it, and YouTube may still store things in the browser.

faq.question: What if the visitor's browser blocks scripts?
faq.answer: They are given a plain link to watch the video on YouTube.
